A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Vision-R1 and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. The shared content can be reliably matched across the revised layout, numbering, and appendix placement.

before.justification: V1 reports original Vision-R1 benchmark results, training-strategy ablations, dataset analyses, and generated reasoning examples in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: V3 retains the original empirical work and adds larger-model evaluations, DynaMath scores, and targeted PTST and cold-start experiments.

M1.justification: The modality-bridging pipeline, cold-start SFT, GRPO objective, hard formatting-and-correctness reward, and progressive length restriction remain unchanged. The larger Qwen models use the existing procedure; their sizes and extended training are experimental-setting changes.

E1.justification: V3 adds DynaMath evaluation in Table 1 and expands RL training coverage with pre-2024 AIME questions rendered as images and subsets of MAmmoTH-VL and MMIQ (Appendix A). This substantially extends the represented training material and input conditions alongside the additional benchmark. The original cold-start sources, three math benchmarks, and four general benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Qwen2.5-VL-32B as a comparator while retaining the previous external comparison methods. Tables 5–6 also introduce internal comparison variants involving alternative PTST schedules and cold-start choices. The Llama-based dataset-quality comparison retains its comparator membership.

E3.justification: V3 adds 32B/72B configurations using approximately 20K additional RL examples and continued Stage 2 training. New ablations vary length limits, sampling counts, and stage schedules, with best-checkpoint selection every five steps during the final 50 steps. Table 1 averages incorporate DynaMath where available. Appendix A also corrects the stated Stage 1 limit from v1's 8K to 4K, aligning it with the existing method description without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Tables 5–6 test fixed versus progressive length limits, sampling counts, an intermediate training stage, PTST without cold start, and SFT without CoT annotations before RL. These substantially expand the original four-variant ablation into targeted tests of schedule design and cold-start content. The modality-bridging example and supplementary reasoning examples are retained, not new analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated independent runs, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V3's best-checkpoint selection procedure changes evaluation practice but does not add uncertainty quantification.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds DynaMath results and larger-model results, including MathVista scores of 76.4 and 78.2 for 32B and 72B models trained with additional data. The original 7B scores of 73.5, 52.4, and 40.2 on MathVista, MathVerse, and MM-Math remain unchanged; its average changes from 55.4 to 55.6 because benchmark coverage expands. Tables 5–6 add control results, and Mulberry-Llama-11B's MMStar score changes from 51.3 to 58.5 (v1 Table 3; v3 Table 2).

T1.justification: Equations 1–2 retain the same GRPO and stage-constrained objectives, advantage calculation, KL expression, and output-space definition. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs, including in the appendices.

C1.justification: V3 narrows the introduction's novelty claim from the first work applying RL to enhance MLLM reasoning to an early exploration of R1-like RL. It also adds headline claims about 32B/72B performance and approximately 10-point average improvements over their base models. The central cold-start, PTST, and 7B reasoning contributions remain.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 softens the description of extended RL-only training from significant performance degradation to no significant improvement. Section 4.2 adds interpretations that complex CoT priors are essential and a simple two-stage PTST schedule is robust. Appendix B further explains why naive captions omit reasoning-relevant visual details. The original overthinking explanation and resource-related qualifications remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly specifies Vision-R1-Zero's 4K limit, 16 samples, and 300 steps, and documents additional-data preparation and larger-model training continuation. However, it removes v1's H800 GPU counts and preparation/SFT/RL runtimes. The abstract adds model weights to the promised code/data release; both versions still describe a future release rather than establish availability.

R1.justification: V3 adds references to MAmmoTH-VL and MM-IQ and moderates its priority claim to an early R1-like RL exploration. The related-work discussion and positioning against existing multimodal CoT approaches otherwise remain substantially unchanged. The switch to author–year citations is presentational.

P1.justification: Most introductory, methodological, and concluding prose is retained. Experimental settings move to Appendix A, dataset-quality analysis and visualization are grouped under ablations, and brief explanatory and LLM-usage appendices are added. Local wording, terminology, author information, and citation-style edits accompany this contained reorganization.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column layout to a predominantly single-column conference format, extensively resizing and repositioning displays. Table 1 gains benchmark columns, larger-model rows, and improvement rows; two new ablation tables are added. All seven figures remain, with v1 Figure 3 moved to Appendix B as v3 Figure 5, and the other retained tables are reordered.

improvement.justification: Tables 5–6 provide more targeted evidence about PTST schedules and cold-start choices, while Table 1 extends evaluation across model scales and another benchmark. Correcting the Stage 1 description also improves consistency. These gains are qualified by removed hardware/runtime disclosures and reporting problems: the new 32B MathVista gain is listed as 4.7 although 76.4 minus 72.9 is 3.5, and Section 4.1 retains 7B ranking claims that no longer match the expanded table. The net improvement is useful but limited.
